questions.q: This small cylindrical hollow punch (0.7–1.2 mm) is used in hair transplantation to extract individual follicular units from the donor scalp without a linear scar. What is the technique called?
opts: FUT punch — Follicular Unit Transplantation; creates a linear scar
ARTAS punch — Automated Robotic Transplant Absorption System
DHI punch — Direct Hair Implantation using a Choi pen
FUE punch — Follicular Unit Extraction; leaves punctate scars, no linear scar
questions.exp:
FUE (Follicular Unit Extraction) uses a sharp hollow punch (0.7–1.2 mm) to score around each follicular unit and extract it directly from the donor area. This leaves only small circular scars (<1 mm) that are virtually invisible even with short hair. FUT (strip harvesting) leaves a linear scar. The Choi implanter pen is used in DHI to place grafts simultaneously without pre-made recipient sites.
🏰 Palace: A COOKIE CUTTER (FUE punch, 0.7–1.2 mm) stamps tiny circles in the CASTLE GARDEN — each stamp takes one follicular family unit, leaving only dot-sized marks.

questions.q: Intralesional 5-fluorouracil (5-FU) reduces hypertrophic scar and keloid bulk by targeting fibroblasts via:
opts: Thymidylate synthase inhibition blocking pyrimidine synthesis and fibroblast DNA replication
Caspase-3-mediated apoptosis of keloid fibroblasts via mitochondrial pathway
Chelation of TGF-β1 in the scar extracellular matrix
Activation of MMP-1 (collagenase) via TNF-α upregulation
questions.exp:
5-FU is a pyrimidine analogue that inhibits thymidylate synthase (the enzyme that converts dUMP to dTMP), preventing DNA synthesis in rapidly proliferating cells. Keloid fibroblasts are hyperproliferative; 5-FU arrests their cell cycle in S-phase. It is often combined with intralesional triamcinolone acetonide (TAC) for synergistic effect. 50mg/mL concentration; injected monthly.
🏰 Palace: 5-FU steals the THYMIDINE BLUEPRINT from keloid fibroblasts' DNA COPY MACHINE (thymidylate synthase) — without the LETTER T in their genetic alphabet, the SCAR SCRIBES cannot write new COLLAGEN CHAPTERS.

questions.q: In hair transplantation, FUT (follicular unit transplantation/strip) has which advantage over FUE for a large single-session graft harvest?
opts: FUT can yield 3000–6000+ grafts per session with lower transection rate, as the surgeon directly visualises follicle anatomy under stereomicroscope
FUE always yields more grafts than FUT in a single session
FUT is preferred for body hair transplantation
FUT uses a 0.8mm punch to extract individual units, same as FUE
questions.exp:
FUT (strip harvesting): A strip of scalp 1–2cm wide is excised from the permanent zone, then individual follicular units are dissected under stereomicroscope by trained technicians. This allows harvesting 3000–6000+ grafts in one session with transection rates <5% (lower than FUE's 5–20%). Disadvantage: linear scar. FUE: individual punch extraction, no linear scar, but more time-consuming and higher transection rates.
🏰 Palace: FUT is STRIP MINING — one LINEAR TRENCH yields THOUSANDS of WHOLE GEMS (low transection) that a microscope team cuts precisely; FUE is INDIVIDUAL GOLD PANNING — slower, leaves no scar but CHIPS more gems during extraction.

questions.q: Striae rubrae (active/red stretch marks) respond better to treatment than striae alba (white/mature). Which laser shows the best evidence for striae rubrae?
opts: CO2 ablative laser — best for all striae types
Pulsed dye laser (PDL, 585/595nm) — targets vascular component of early striae
Q-switched Nd:YAG 1064nm — targets pigment in striae rubrae
Er:YAG — best for striae alba due to ablative remodelling
questions.exp:
Striae rubrae are erythematous due to active dermal vascularity and perivascular inflammation — this vascular component makes PDL 585/595nm highly effective (targets oxyhemoglobin). PDL also stimulates collagen remodelling in the dermis. Striae alba lack this vascular component, making PDL less effective; fractional CO2 or Er:YAG are better for mature white striae (ablative remodelling).
🏰 Palace: STRIAE RUBRAE = RED WOUNDS with BLOOD VESSELS — PDL PURPLE VAMPIRE feeds on red striae perfectly; STRIAE ALBA are old GREY SCARS without blood, so PDL is useless — use the ABLATIVE DRILL (CO2) instead.

questions.q: Picosecond lasers (e.g., PicoSure 755nm) offer which advantage over conventional nanosecond Q-switched lasers for tattoo removal?
opts: Picosecond pulses penetrate deeper into the dermis
Photoacoustic effect dominates over photothermal, fragmenting ink into smaller particles requiring fewer sessions
Picosecond lasers require lower fluences reducing side effects significantly
Picosecond lasers target a broader spectrum of ink colors than Q-switched
questions.exp:
Picosecond lasers (10⁻¹² s) deliver energy faster than the thermal relaxation time of ink particles, creating dominant photoacoustic (pressure/shock wave) effects vs the photothermal mechanism of nanosecond QS lasers. This shatters ink into much smaller fragments (easier macrophage clearance), achieving better clearance with fewer sessions, especially for resistant blue/green inks and recalcitrant tattoos.
🏰 Palace: PICO is the SONIC BOOM weapon — it creates SHOCKWAVES that SHATTER ink into DUST, while ns Q-switched is a HEAT GUN that melts ink into GRAVEL — fewer sessions to clear the tattoo dungeon.

questions.q: Erbium:YAG laser (2940nm) compared to CO2 laser (10600nm) for ablative skin resurfacing is characterised by:
opts: Greater coagulation haemostasis, better for vascular lesions
Deeper tissue penetration per pulse, superior for deep acne scars
Identical ablation depth but superior collagen remodelling
~16× greater water absorption, more precise ablation, less thermal necrosis/coagulation
questions.exp:
Er:YAG at 2940nm is at the peak of water absorption (coefficient ~12,000 cm⁻¹), approximately 16× higher than CO2 (10600nm, ~800 cm⁻¹). This results in very precise ablation of 5–20μm per pulse with minimal thermal spread (5–50μm vs CO2's 100–150μm zone of necrosis). Less post-procedure redness and faster healing, but less collagen remodelling than CO2.
🏰 Palace: ER:YAG is the PRECISION SURGEON — 16× MORE THIRSTY for water, it ablates EXACTLY its target with MINIMAL CHAR BURN, while CO2 is the BIGGER HAMMER that leaves a warm zone of extra cooking.

questions.q: Topical retinol undergoes sequential enzymatic conversion in skin. The correct pathway sequence is:
opts: Retinol → retinyl ester → all-trans retinoic acid
Retinol → retinaldehyde (retinal) → all-trans retinoic acid (tretinoin)
Retinol → retinoic acid → retinal → retinyl palmitate
Retinol → β-carotene → retinoic acid
questions.exp:
Retinol is oxidised to retinaldehyde (retinal) by retinol dehydrogenases (RDH), then retinal is irreversibly oxidised to all-trans retinoic acid (tretinoin, the active form) by retinaldehyde dehydrogenases (RALDH). This two-step conversion means retinol is approximately 20× less potent than tretinoin but causes less irritation. Retinyl esters (palmitate, acetate) are the least potent — they must first be hydrolysed back to retinol.
🏰 Palace: RETINOL climbs TWO CASTLE STAIRS: first to the RETINAL FLOOR (oxidation #1), then to the RETINOIC ACID THRONE ROOM (oxidation #2) — retinyl esters are in the BASEMENT and must take 3 flights.

questions.q: LED photobiomodulation for skin uses different wavelengths. Match: Blue (415nm), Red (633nm), Near-infrared (830nm) to their primary dermatological effects:
opts: Blue = porphyrin photoactivation killing P. acnes (anti-acne); Red = collagen stimulation/anti-inflammatory; NIR = deep tissue healing/wound repair
Blue = collagen synthesis; Red = anti-acne; NIR = pigmentation reduction
All three wavelengths have identical mechanisms, differing only in depth of penetration
Blue = anti-inflammatory; Red = melanogenesis stimulation; NIR = acne treatment
questions.exp:
LED wavelength effects: 415nm (blue) — activates endogenous porphyrins in Cutibacterium acnes producing singlet oxygen; 633nm (red) — absorbed by cytochrome c oxidase, stimulates ATP/collagen, anti-inflammatory (reduces IL-1β, TNF-α, PGE2); 830nm (near-infrared) — deepest penetration (5–10mm), promotes wound healing, reduces inflammation in deeper tissues. Often combined in dual/multi-wavelength devices.
🏰 Palace: LED TRAFFIC SIGNALS: BLUE (415nm) ARRESTS ACNE BACTERIA, RED (633nm) REPAIRS THE SKIN MOTORWAY (collagen, anti-inflammation), NIR (830nm) GOES UNDERGROUND to fix the deep DUNGEON FLOOR (wound healing).

questions.q: This laser emits 755 nm wavelength and is considered the gold standard for laser hair removal in Fitzpatrick skin types I–III due to its high melanin selectivity. What is its primary chromophore in hair follicle targeting?
opts: Alexandrite laser — haemoglobin in follicular vasculature
Alexandrite laser (755 nm) — melanin in the bulge/bulb region of the hair follicle
Alexandrite laser — keratin in the hair shaft cortex
Alexandrite laser — water in the follicular shaft
questions.exp:
The alexandrite laser (755 nm) has very high melanin absorption compared to other hair removal lasers. It targets melanin in the matrix cells of the hair bulb and stem cells in the bulge, thermally destroying the follicle. Long-pulse mode with pulse durations equal to or less than the TRT of the hair follicle (~40–100 ms) achieves selective follicular destruction. Best for skin types I–III.
🏰 Palace: ALEXANDRITE ARCHER (755 nm) fires melanin-seeking arrows deep into the HAIR BULGE CASTLE — only DARK-WALLED follicles get hit, leaving fair-skinned epidermal walls unscathed.

questions.q: Biostimulators (PLLA, CaHA, PMMA) differ fundamentally from volumising fillers (HA, collagen) in that:
opts: Biostimulators provide immediate volume through high osmotic water attraction; fillers work slowly
Biostimulators are reversible with hyaluronidase; fillers (HA) are not
Biostimulators work primarily through neocollagenesis with a delayed effect over months; fillers provide immediate volume via hydrophilic gel/space-filling
Both mechanisms are identical — the distinction is regulatory only
questions.exp:
Biostimulators (collagen stimulators): PLLA microspheres and CaHA particles act as a scaffold, inducing a controlled foreign-body response that drives fibroblast activation and neocollagenesis. The initial carrier gel absorbs over weeks; long-term volume comes from new collagen (3–6 months). HA fillers: immediate volume from the hydrophilic gel (cross-linked HA holds water) with no significant collagen stimulation.
🏰 Palace: BIOSTIMULATORS plant SEEDS in the CASTLE GARDEN that GROW COLLAGEN TREES over months; TRUE FILLERS are INSTANT WATER BALLOONS inflated on the spot — one is a slow HARVEST, the other is a FAST PUMP.

questions.q: In the second centrifugation step of the double-spin PRP preparation technique, the primary purpose is:
opts: Concentrating platelets from the buffy coat layer into a small volume by spinning down residual red cells and separating platelet-poor plasma
Separating red blood cells from plasma (that is the role of the first spin)
Removing white blood cells to reduce inflammatory cytokines
Activating platelets by mechanical stress of the centrifuge
questions.exp:
Double-spin PRP: First spin (soft spin, ~200–400g, 10 min) separates RBCs from plasma + platelets (buffy coat). The platelet-rich layer (buffy coat + platelet-rich plasma above it) is carefully aspirated. Second spin (hard spin, ~400–800g, 10 min) concentrates platelets into a pellet at the bottom, and platelet-poor plasma (PPP) above is removed, leaving concentrated PRP.
🏰 Palace: PRP DOUBLE SPIN: FIRST SPIN separates RED ARMY (RBCs) to the DUNGEON FLOOR; SECOND SPIN SQUEEZES the PLATELET GOLD from the buffy coat into a tiny CONCENTRATED TREASURE CHEST at the bottom.

questions.q: In spironolactone use for female pattern hair loss, the primary mechanism of action is:
opts: Inhibits 5-alpha reductase type 2 in dermal papilla cells
Androgen receptor antagonist in hair follicle dermal papilla cells, blocking DHT binding and downstream miniaturisation signals
Reduces DHT production by blocking CYP17A1 in the adrenal cortex
Directly activates the Wnt/β-catenin pathway in follicle stem cells
questions.exp:
Spironolactone is a competitive aldosterone antagonist with potent androgen receptor (AR) antagonist properties. At the hair follicle level, it blocks DHT and testosterone from binding to the AR in dermal papilla cells, preventing DHT-driven follicular miniaturisation. It also weakly inhibits 5-alpha reductase. Effective dose for FPHL: 50–200mg/day. Avoid in women planning pregnancy (feminises male fetuses).
🏰 Palace: SPIRONOLACTONE is the ANDROGEN RECEPTOR BODYGUARD who BLOCKS DHT from entering the DERMAL PAPILLA THRONE ROOM — DHT can't bind, can't send the MINIATURISATION ORDER, hair follicles survive.

questions.q: The 'Nefertiti lift' uses botulinum toxin to redefine the jawline and neck. Which muscles are injected?
opts: Sternocleidomastoid and digastric
Platysmal cervical bands and depressor anguli oris
Mentalis and orbicularis oris
Masseter and buccinator
questions.exp:
The Nefertiti lift targets the platysma (cervical bands at the jawline level) and depressor anguli oris (DAO). Weakening these downward-pulling muscles allows the zygomaticus and other elevators to dominate, lifting and defining the lower face and jawline. 2–4 U per injection point along the mandibular border and upper platysma.
🏰 Palace: NEFERTITI's SHARP JAWLINE was sculpted by CUTTING THE ROPES (platysma + DAO) that pulled her face DOWN — toxin scissors snip the depressor cables, letting the ELEVATOR GODS lift the jaw.

questions.q: The Monheit combination medium-depth chemical peel applies two agents in sequence. What is the combination and what is its depth of penetration?
opts: Glycolic acid 70% + TCA 50% — penetrates to subcutis
Jessner's solution + TCA 35% — penetrates to upper reticular dermis
Jessner's + glycolic acid 30% — penetrates to papillary dermis only
Phenol 50% + TCA 35% — penetrates to deep reticular dermis
questions.exp:
The Monheit combination peel uses Jessner's solution (to strip the stratum corneum barrier uniformly) followed immediately by TCA 35%. Jessner's creates a uniform exfoliation that allows TCA to penetrate evenly into the papillary-upper reticular dermis. This gives more predictable medium-depth results than TCA 35% alone, with Jessner's also reducing the risk of TCA frosting irregularities.
🏰 Palace: MONHEIT's DOUBLE AGENT: JESSNER strips the CASTLE GATE (SC) first, then TCA 35% FLOODS through the OPEN GATE into the papillary-reticular dungeon — more even, more reliable than TCA alone.

questions.q: Which ingredient is NOT a component of classic (original) Jessner's solution?
opts: Glycolic acid
Resorcinol (14%)
Lactic acid (14%)
Salicylic acid (14%)
questions.exp:
Classic Jessner's solution (Combes-Jessner formula, 1941) contains resorcinol 14g, salicylic acid 14g, and lactic acid 14g in 95% ethanol to make 100mL. Glycolic acid is NOT a component of the original formula. Modified Jessner's solutions may substitute resorcinol with glycolic acid (to avoid resorcinol's risk of thyroid disruption) but this is a distinct formulation.
🏰 Palace: JESSNER'S ORIGINAL TRIO: RESORCINOL (R) + SALICYLIC ACID (S) + LACTIC ACID (L) = RSL in ethanol — GLYCOLIC ACID applied for the ORIGINAL JOB but was REJECTED; it only gets into MODIFIED Jessner's.

questions.q: The risk of neutralizing antibody (NAb) formation to botulinum toxin type A is highest with which injection pattern?
opts: Low dose with high frequency spaced 6-monthly intervals
Single large-dose treatment yearly
High cumulative dose with short inter-treatment intervals (<12 weeks)
Use of preservative-free saline for reconstitution
questions.exp:
Neutralizing antibodies to BoNT-A develop due to exposure to the 900-kDa complexing proteins (hemagglutinins) associated with the toxin. Risk is highest with: (1) high cumulative doses, (2) booster injections within 4–12 weeks ('top-up' injections), and (3) old formulations with higher protein loads. Onabotulinumtoxin A and abobotulinumtoxin A have higher protein loads than incobotulinumtoxin A (Xeomin, protein-free).
🏰 Palace: ANTIBODY ARMY mobilises when TOXIN INVADES FREQUENTLY (short intervals) and in LARGE BATTALIONS (high dose) — the immune CASTLE sees too much PROTEIN and builds a NEUTRALISING SHIELD.

questions.q: After fractional CO₂ resurfacing, milia formation as a complication occurs due to:
opts: Deep penetration destroying the sebaceous glands, leaving empty follicles
Laser-induced melanocyte migration forming epidermal cysts
Occlusive post-procedure dressings/ointments obstructing follicular infundibula during re-epithelialisation
Bacterial superinfection of microcolumns of thermal injury
questions.exp:
Milia (retention cysts) after fractional CO2 resurfacing form because occlusive post-procedure ointments (petrolatum, white soft paraffin) block the follicular infundibula during the healing phase. Trapped keratin forms small white inclusion cysts (milia). Treatment: gentle extraction with a fine lancet. Prevention: open wound care (no heavy occlusives) and use of lighter barrier creams during healing.
🏰 Palace: MILIA AFTER LASER = KERATIN TRAPPED in follicle DOORS sealed by HEAVY OINTMENT — like using too much MORTAR on the new castle stones, it blocks the VENTILATION SHAFTS and traps dead skin inside.

questions.q: The 'Sinclair scale' for female pattern hair loss (FPHL) differs from Ludwig classification in that:
opts: Both scales are interchangeable with no meaningful clinical difference
Sinclair measures hair pull test results; Ludwig measures dermoscopic findings
Sinclair applies only to postmenopausal women; Ludwig applies to all ages
Sinclair is a 5-grade photographic scale including frontal hairline recession; Ludwig focuses on vertex/crown diffuse thinning only
questions.exp:
Ludwig (1977): 3-stage scale for female AGA — stage I (minimal), II (moderate), III (extensive) crown/vertex thinning with preserved frontal hairline. Sinclair (2004): 5-stage scale including frontal hairline, midscalp, and vertex zones, capturing the full spectrum of FPHL. The Sinclair scale is more sensitive for early and advanced disease and is recommended by current guidelines as the preferred clinical staging tool.
🏰 Palace: SINCLAIR is the BIGGER 5-FLOOR CASTLE (5 grades, includes FRONTAL + CROWN); LUDWIG is a SMALLER 3-ROOM COTTAGE (3 grades, VERTEX ONLY) — both measure FPHL but Sinclair sees MORE of the castle.

questions.q: Kojic acid reduces melanin synthesis by which molecular mechanism?
opts: Upregulating proteasomal degradation of tyrosinase protein
Competitively inhibiting tyrosinase at the L-DOPA binding site
Chelating copper ions in the active site of tyrosinase, inhibiting enzymatic activity
Blocking melanosome transfer from melanocytes to keratinocytes
questions.exp:
Kojic acid (5-hydroxy-2-hydroxymethyl-4H-pyran-4-one) chelates the two copper ions in the active site of tyrosinase, rendering the enzyme catalytically inactive. It does not compete at the substrate-binding site. Effective at 1–4% concentrations. More unstable than hydroquinone; often combined with glycolic acid or vitamin C. Associated with contact dermatitis in some users.
🏰 Palace: KOJIC ACID is the COPPER PICKPOCKET — it steals the TWO COPPER COINS from TYROSINASE's pockets, leaving the enzyme BROKE and unable to convert DOPA to melanin.

questions.q: Narrowband UVB (NB-UVB, 311nm) is superior to broadband UVB (BB-UVB, 280–320nm) for psoriasis and vitiligo because:
opts: NB-UVB penetrates to the deep reticular dermis unlike BB-UVB which reaches only the epidermis
311nm is the optimal immunosuppressive/therapeutic wavelength, while BB-UVB includes carcinogenic shorter wavelengths (<295nm) that increase side effects
NB-UVB activates vitamin D synthesis more efficiently than BB-UVB
NB-UVB avoids all erythemal wavelengths, eliminating sunburn risk
questions.exp:
The erythemal action spectrum peaks around 295–300nm. NB-UVB at 311nm is at the optimal immunosuppressive-to-erythemogenic ratio. BB-UVB includes wavelengths <295nm (UVC-range) that are maximally erythemal and carcinogenic but have little therapeutic benefit. By delivering only the 311nm band, NB-UVB achieves better efficacy with less erythema and lower cumulative carcinogenic load.
🏰 Palace: NB-UVB SNIPER hits 311nm SWEET SPOT — therapeutic without BURNING; BB-UVB is a SCATTERGUN that hits 280nm DANGER ZONE (carcinogenic) unnecessarily. Same castle, better aim.

questions.q: Rosacea subtype 1 (erythematotelangiectatic rosacea, ETR) with persistent erythema and telangiectasias responds best to:
opts: Pulsed dye laser (PDL 585/595nm) or KTP laser (532nm) targeting cutaneous vascular component
NB-UVB phototherapy for anti-inflammatory effect
Oral metronidazole as first-line for telangiectasias
Retinoids to reduce sebaceous hyperactivity
questions.exp:
ETR (subtype 1) rosacea is primarily a vascular disorder with flushing, persistent erythema, and telangiectasias. Vascular-specific lasers target the haemoglobin chromophore: PDL 585/595nm and KTP 532nm are first-line laser treatments. IPL (560nm cut-off filter) is also effective. Multiple sessions typically needed. Oral doxycycline and topical brimonidine/oxymetazoline address flushing and erythema but do not remove telangiectasias.
🏰 Palace: ETR ROSACEA's RED RIVERS (telangiectasias) need VASCULAR LASERS to block them — PDL PURPLE VAMPIRE (595nm) or KTP GREEN SNIPER (532nm) both hunt oxyhaemoglobin in the red vessel network.

questions.q: Cross-linked hyaluronic acid fillers use 1,4-butanediol diglycidyl ether (BDDE) as the cross-linker. The degree of cross-linking affects which filler property most directly?
opts: Colour — higher cross-linking → transparent appearance
Longevity and cohesivity — higher cross-linking → harder gel, longer lasting, more lift capacity
Osmotic swelling — more cross-linking → more hygroscopic
Reversibility with hyaluronidase — more cross-linking → impossible to dissolve
questions.exp:
BDDE cross-linking creates ether bonds between HA chains, reducing their susceptibility to hyaluronidase degradation and increasing gel stiffness (G' elastic modulus). Higher G' = more cohesive, longer-lasting filler able to withstand mechanical forces (lifting heavy tissue). Lower G' = softer, more spreadable filler (e.g., for fine lines). All BDDE-cross-linked fillers remain dissolvable with hyaluronidase.
🏰 Palace: BDDE is the CASTLE ARCHITECT welding HA CHAINS with epoxide bridges — MORE BRIDGES = STRONGER WALLS (harder gel, lasts longer), but even the strongest HA castle melts when HYALURONIDASE FIRE arrives.

questions.q: Post-sclerotherapy hyperpigmentation (PSH) is caused by:
opts: Melanocyte stimulation by the sclerosant chemical
Direct injection of sclerosant into dermal melanocytes causing pigment release
UV-induced post-inflammatory hyperpigmentation in the treated area
Haemosiderin deposition from extravascular red blood cell breakdown in the treated vessel
questions.exp:
Post-sclerotherapy hyperpigmentation occurs in ~10–30% of treated patients. Mechanism: sclerosant-induced endothelial damage causes red blood cell extravasation (haemolysis) into the perivascular tissue. Haemoglobin breaks down to haemosiderin, which deposits in the dermis, causing a brownish discolouration. Resolves over 6–24 months in most cases. Risk factors: higher concentration sclerosant, thrombosis, inadequate compression post-treatment.
🏰 Palace: PSH RUST STAIN: treated vein LEAKS RED BLOOD CELLS → haemoglobin breaks down to HAEMOSIDERIN RUST that STAINS the DERMIS FLOOR brown — like rust rings in a CASTLE DRAINPIPE after the water treatment.

questions.q: Glycolic acid achieves effective epidermolysis and comedolysis in acne at which minimum parameters?
opts: ≥20% concentration at pH <4 (free acid determines activity, not total glycolic acid content)
70% concentration regardless of pH is the minimum effective dose
5–10% concentration at pH 5–6 is sufficient for acne treatment
Any concentration above 1% has equal therapeutic efficacy
questions.exp:
Glycolic acid (AHA) activity depends on free acid concentration (not just total %): free acid = total acid × proportion in undissociated form = varies with pH. At pH 3–4, most is undissociated (active). Minimum effective: 20–30% total glycolic acid at pH ≤3.5 for peeling effects. At neutral pH (pH 7), even 70% glycolic acid has minimal penetration because it is fully ionised and cannot cross the SC lipid barrier.
🏰 Palace: GLYCOLIC ACID needs to be STRONG (≥20%) AND ACIDIC (pH<4 gate) — a NEUTRAL PH GLYCOLIC ACID is like a LOCKED CASTLE ARMY: even 70% can't break through because the acid IONISES and loses its SC-crossing PASSPORT.

questions.q: After botulinum toxin injection into the glabellar complex, a patient develops unilateral eyelid ptosis 3 days later. The most likely mechanism is:
opts: Systemic absorption causing generalized neuromuscular blockade
Toxin migration through the orbital septum affecting the levator palpebrae superioris
Haematoma compression of the oculomotor nerve
Direct injection into the orbicularis oculi
questions.exp:
Eyelid ptosis is the most feared complication of glabellar BoNT-A injection. It occurs due to toxin diffusion through the orbital septum reaching the levator palpebrae superioris (LPS). Risk is minimised by injecting >1cm above the orbital rim and by avoiding excessive volumes. Apraclonidine 0.5% eye drops (α-agonist stimulating Müller's muscle) can partially reverse ptosis.
🏰 Palace: PTOSIS GHOST drifts through the ORBITAL SEPTUM GHOST DOOR — it wasn't meant to reach the LEVATOR CABLE (LPS) but bad injection site lets it slip through and DROP the eyelid curtain.

questions.q: Intralesional triamcinolone acetonide (ILT) for keloids: what is the recommended concentration range and injection frequency?
opts: 0.5 mg/mL daily injection for 6 weeks
10–40 mg/mL injected every 4–6 weeks until flattening achieved
80 mg/mL single injection only
1–5 mg/mL injected weekly for 3 months
questions.exp:
Intralesional triamcinolone acetonide is first-line for keloids: 10 mg/mL for small/soft keloids, 20–40 mg/mL for thick/resistant keloids. Injected every 4–6 weeks. Mechanism: inhibits fibroblast proliferation, reduces TGF-β and collagen synthesis, causes collagen degradation. Side effects at high doses include skin atrophy, telangiectasias, and depigmentation.
🏰 Palace: TRIAMCINOLONE FLOOD for keloids: 10mg/mL for BABY KELOIDS, 40mg/mL for FORTRESS KELOIDS — flood the castle every 4–6 WEEKS until the OVERBUILT WALLS crumble (flatten), but beware of ATROPHY MOAT (over-flooding causes skin thinning).

questions.q: A 'chemical brow lift' with botulinum toxin is achieved by targeting which muscle, and what is the anatomical rationale?
opts: Corrugator supercilii — its relaxation lifts the medial brow arch
Procerus — its relaxation removes medial brow depression
Frontalis — its selective medial weakening elevates the lateral segment
Lateral orbicularis oculi (brow depressor) — its paralysis allows the unopposed frontalis to elevate the lateral brow
questions.exp:
The lateral brow depressor is the lateral orbicularis oculi (specifically the supraorbital portion). By injecting 2–4U into this muscle approximately 1cm lateral to the orbital rim, its downward pull is reduced. The frontalis (unopposed elevator) then lifts the lateral brow, creating a subtle arch — the classic 'Botox brow lift'. Injecting medial frontalis raises the medial peak, while lateral injection raises the tail.
🏰 Palace: BROW LIFT TRICK: shoot LATERAL ORBICULARIS (brow BOUNCER who pushes it DOWN) with toxin — FRONTALIS ELEVATOR (the CRANE) then PULLS the lateral brow UP unopposed, creating the MODEL ARCH.

questions.q: In mechanical dermabrasion for acne scars, the clinical endpoint that signals reaching the correct depth for rolling/boxcar scars is:
opts: Grey-white pebbly surface indicating deep reticular dermis
Pinpoint punctate bleeding indicating the papillary-reticular dermal junction
Yellow fat globules indicating subcutaneous fat
Cessation of bleeding due to reflex vasoconstriction
questions.exp:
Dermabrasion endpoints: (1) fine stippling with very mild oozing = epidermis only; (2) pinpoint bleeding = papillary dermis (safe endpoint for most indications including acne scars); (3) brisk bleeding = reticular dermis (excessive — risk of scarring); (4) yellow fat = subcutaneous (danger zone). For rolling/boxcar scars, the endpoint is pinpoint bleeding with effacement of the scar edges.
🏰 Palace: DERMABRASION TRAFFIC LIGHTS: PINK STIPPLE = green (epidermis), PINPOINT RED DOTS = amber (STOP HERE for acne scars, papillary dermis), BRISK BLEEDING = red (gone too deep!), YELLOW FAT = emergency stop.

questions.q: Niacinamide (vitamin B3) reduces skin hyperpigmentation primarily by:
opts: Inhibiting melanosome transfer from melanocytes to keratinocytes via SNAP-23/vesicle fusion inhibition
Directly inhibiting tyrosinase at the copper active site
Chelating zinc required for tyrosinase cofactor activity
Blocking MSH receptors (MC1R) on melanocytes
questions.exp:
Niacinamide inhibits the transfer of melanosomes from melanocytes to keratinocytes. This is the key step where packaged melanin is delivered to the overlying keratinocytes that actually produce skin colour. Niacinamide at 2–5% significantly reduces transfer efficiency, leading to visible brightening over 4–8 weeks. It does not inhibit melanin synthesis itself, so it is safe and non-cytotoxic to melanocytes.
🏰 Palace: NIACINAMIDE is the TOLL BOOTH GUARD who BLOCKS the MELANOSOME DELIVERY VAN from crossing the melanocyte-keratinocyte border — the melanin packages stay STUCK on the factory side.

questions.q: The 'Hollywood peel' (carbon laser peel) combines topical carbon paste with Q-switched Nd:YAG 1064nm. The mechanism of comedolysis/exfoliation is:
opts: Carbon acts as a photosensitiser generating singlet oxygen to oxidise keratinocytes
Carbon cream acts as a chemical exfoliant independent of the laser component
Carbon absorbs 1064nm energy and rapidly vaporises, causing photomechanical exfoliation of stratum corneum and comedone contents
The Nd:YAG heats the dermis while carbon reflects the laser preventing epidermal damage

Rapid energy absorption causes rapid heating and vaporisation (photomechanical/photothermal effect), which mechanically exfoliates the SC and dislodges sebum/comedone plugs. questions.q: This cylindrical cutting instrument creates a full-thickness skin biopsy from epidermis to subcutaneous fat. What sizes (in mm) are recommended for routine diagnostic biopsy versus larger excision?
opts: Shave biopsy — 2 mm for diagnosis, 4 mm for excision
Punch biopsy — 3–4 mm for diagnosis, 6–8 mm for complete excision of small lesions
Dermal curette — 5 mm standard for all lesions
Trephine — 10 mm minimum for diagnosis
questions.exp:

questions.q: A 27-year-old woman with Fitzpatrick III skin has 2-year-old bilateral symmetric malar and centrofacial melasma refractory to topical triple combination therapy. The most appropriate next step is:
opts: Q-switched Nd:YAG laser toning as monotherapy replacing topicals
Microneedling with vitamin C serum as the sole treatment
Oral tranexamic acid (250mg twice daily) as systemic adjunct, with continued topical treatment
Ablative CO2 laser resurfacing for deeper dermal melanin
questions.exp:

Mechanism: inhibits UV-induced prostaglandin synthesis in keratinocytes, reducing c-kit ligand/stem cell factor which activates melanocytes. Also directly inhibits plasminogen activator. It is particularly effective for mixed dermal-epidermal melasma refractory to topicals. Side effects: GI upset, rare thrombosis risk (caution in high-risk patients).

questions.q: This pre-filled syringe contains calcium hydroxylapatite (CaHA) microspheres suspended in carboxymethylcellulose gel. When used for facial volume restoration, what additional unique property distinguishes it from HA fillers?
opts: CaHA filler — reversible with hyaluronidase like HA fillers
CaHA filler — biodegradable in 2 weeks with no collagen effect
CaHA filler (Radiesse) — stimulates de novo collagen production (biostimulator) in addition to immediate volume; not reversible with hyaluronidase
CaHA filler — radioopaque and visible on X-ray with no soft-tissue effect
questions.exp:

The gel provides immediate volume; as it is absorbed over ~3 months, the CaHA particles stimulate fibroblasts to produce new collagen and elastin (biostimulator effect) lasting 12–18 months. Unlike HA fillers, CaHA cannot be dissolved with hyaluronidase. It is radiopaque and visible on plain X-rays.

questions.q: Paradoxical adipose hyperplasia (PAH) after cryolipolysis is characterised by:
opts: Painless, firm enlargement of the treatment area 2–4 months post-treatment; more common in males; requires liposuction for correction
Fat cell necrosis leading to visible dimpling 1 week after treatment
Occurs in 5–10% of patients; resolves spontaneously within 6 months
Painful inflammatory nodules appearing 2 weeks post-treatment; equal gender distribution

It occurs more commonly in males (Hispanic males particularly over-represented). Mechanism unknown — possibly paradoxical cold-induced stimulation of lipogenesis. Treatment: surgical liposuction.
🏰 Palace: PAH is the OPPOSITE TRICK: instead of the fat MELTING, the CRYOLIPOLYSIS castle GROWS BIGGER — a FIRM STONE PRISON forms (0.03% chance) more in MALE CASTLES, and only LIPOSUCTION can DEMOLISH it.

questions.q: Minor's starch-iodine test is used to map hyperhidrotic zones before botulinum toxin injection. What is the sequence and expected positive result?
opts: Apply iodine → UV light illuminates sweat zones → starch is not needed
Apply starch first → then iodine → sweating causes blue-black colour
Apply iodine solution → allow to dry → dust with starch powder → sweat turns mixture dark brown/black indicating active sweating
Inject iodine intradermally → wait 5 minutes → dark spots indicate eccrine gland density
questions.exp:

When sweat is secreted, the iodine and starch react (iodine-starch complex) producing a dark brown/black colour at the site of active sweat glands. This maps the exact hyperhidrotic zone for targeted BoNT-A injection (usually 50–100U per axilla).
🏰 Palace: MINOR's MAGIC MAP: paint IODINE on the AXILLA DUNGEON, dust STARCH like talcum powder — each SWEAT DROP turns the starch DARK as a MAGICAL INK DOT, revealing the sweating castle rooms to target.

questions.q: Subcision for rolling acne scars utilises a Nokor (tri-bevelled) needle. The mechanism is:
opts: Injecting saline to hydraulically separate the scar base
Abrading the scar base via the needle tip to stimulate collagen
Cutting fibrous tethers between the scar base and deep dermis/subcutis, releasing the depressed floor
Delivering radiofrequency energy through the needle to remodel collagen
questions.exp:
Subcision involves inserting a Nokor needle parallel to the skin surface under the depressed scar and cutting fibrous tethers anchoring the scar floor to deeper structures. This 'piston' motion releases the scar, allowing it to elevate. The resulting haematoma and wound healing further stimulate collagen deposition. It is most effective for rolling scars and can be combined with PRP or HA fillers.
🏰 Palace: SUBCISION is the UNDERGROUND SWORD STROKE — the Nokor needle sneaks UNDER THE SCAR and SEVERS the ROPE TETHERS holding the floor DOWN; the released floor SPRINGS UP as new collagen fills the tunnel.

questions.q: Electroporation (EP) enhances transdermal drug delivery by which mechanism?
opts: Ultrasound cavitation disrupts intercellular lipids in the SC
Sustained low-voltage current heats the stratum corneum to 45°C melting lipid lamellae
High-voltage (50–500V) millisecond pulses create transient aqueous pores in stratum corneum lipid bilayers
Creates permanent microchannels similar to fractional microneedling
questions.exp:
Electroporation uses brief high-voltage electric pulses (50–500V, 10μs–10ms) to temporarily destabilise the lipid bilayers of cell membranes and the stratum corneum, forming transient aqueous pores. These pores allow passage of large, hydrophilic, and even charged molecules that cannot normally penetrate skin. The pores reseal in milliseconds to seconds after the pulse ends (reversible electroporation).
🏰 Palace: ELECTROPORATION is a LIGHTNING STORM hitting the LIPID CASTLE WALL — each ZAP tears a TEMPORARY WATER GATE through the lipid barrier; drugs SPRINT through before the gate SNAPS SHUT in milliseconds.

questions.q: This bottle contains a peeling solution composed of resorcinol 14%, salicylic acid 14%, and lactic acid 14% in an ethanol base. It is a superficial-to-medium peel. What is it called, and what condition is it classically used for?
opts: Glycolic acid 70% — alpha-hydroxy acid for superficial exfoliation
Phenol peel — deep chemical peel for severe photoaging
Jessner's solution — melasma, acne, post-inflammatory hyperpigmentation; produces even superficial exfoliation
Modified Kligman's formula — contains hydroquinone 4% for melasma only

Resorcinol disrupts hydrogen bonds in keratin; salicylic acid is keratolytic; lactic acid is an AHA providing exfoliation and hydration. It is a reliable superficial peel used for acne vulgaris, melasma, PIH, and actinic damage. It can be layered for medium-depth peeling.
🏰 Palace: JESSNER's CASTLE MIX has THREE GUARDS (resorcinol + SA + LA, each 14%) — they work in EQUAL SHIFTS breaking down the skin's KERATIN GATE for smooth exfoliation of PIH and acne.

questions.q: Q-switched Nd:YAG 1064nm is preferred for which tattoo ink color(s), and why?
opts: Green ink — better than ruby 694nm for green
Yellow ink — only 1064nm can target yellow pigments
Black and dark blue — high 1064nm absorption by carbon-based dark pigments
Red ink — 1064nm coincides with red chromophore absorption peak

For coloured inks: red → KTP 532nm; green → ruby 694nm or alexandrite 755nm; yellow (most resistant) → 532nm. The 1064nm wavelength also penetrates deepest, reaching ink in the deep dermis.

questions.q: Late-onset nodules appearing 8–12 months after poly-L-lactic acid (PLLA / Sculptra) injection are best avoided by:
opts: Adequate reconstitution (≥5mL water per vial, 24–72h hydration) and not injecting too superficially or undiluted
Injecting immediately after reconstitution to prevent settling
Using smaller particle size PLLA (5μm) exclusively for facial use
Adding hyaluronidase to the reconstitution solution to prevent clumping
questions.exp:
PLLA nodules are predominantly technique-related: (1) inadequate dilution (undiluted particles clump); (2) insufficient hydration time (<24h); (3) superficial placement (intradermal instead of deep subcutaneous/supraperiosteal); (4) injection into muscle (causes granulomas). Prevention: dilute to ≥5mL (some use 8–10mL), hydrate 24–72h, inject in supraperiosteal or deep subcutaneous plane, massage 5 × 5 × 5 (5 minutes, 5 times daily, 5 days).
🏰 Palace: SCULPTRA NODULE PREVENTION: give it a LONG BATH (24–72h), DILUTE IT WELL (5–8mL water), inject DEEP in the CASTLE DUNGEON (not the top floor) — rush it DRY into SHALLOW SKIN and NODULE STONES form.

questions.q: In barbed thread lifting, bidirectional (bi-directional cog) threads differ from unidirectional threads in that they:
opts: Require fixation to the deep temporal fascia at one end for anchoring
Must always be used in pairs to cancel unequal pull
Are used exclusively for volume restoration, not mechanical lifting
Are self-anchoring — barbs on both halves face opposite directions gripping tissue from both ends
questions.exp:
Unidirectional cog threads have all barbs facing the same direction; they must be anchored at one end (e.g., deep temporal fascia) for the lift to work. Bidirectional threads have barbs pointing in opposite directions from the mid-point of the thread — the upper half grips tissue moving upward, the lower half anchors going downward, creating a self-locking mechanism without an external anchor point.
🏰 Palace: BIDIRECTIONAL THREAD is a TWO-HEADED FISH HOOK — barbs face BOTH WAYS from the MIDDLE, gripping tissue in OPPOSITE DIRECTIONS without needing to be NAILED to the temple wall.

questions.q: Intra-arterial filler injection causing blindness most commonly occurs via which anatomical pathway?
opts: Carotid artery embolism from the temporal injection site
Central retinal vein occlusion via raised intraorbital pressure
Retrograde embolism through the supratrochlear/dorsal nasal artery into the ophthalmic artery, causing central retinal artery occlusion
Direct injection into the ophthalmic artery via the superior orbit
questions.exp:
When filler is injected into a branch of the ophthalmic artery (supratrochlear, supraorbital, dorsal nasal artery), injection pressure exceeds arterial systolic pressure, driving filler retrograde back toward the ophthalmic artery origin. From there, anterograde flow carries filler into the central retinal artery (CRA), causing CRAO and blindness. The glabella, nose, and nasolabial fold are highest-risk zones due to dense anastomoses with ophthalmic artery branches.
🏰 Palace: BLINDNESS MAP: FILLER fired UPSTREAM into the SUPRATROCHLEAR ARTERY races RETROGRADE back to the OPHTHALMIC ARTERY, then is carried FORWARD into the RETINAL ARTERY — one wrong shot in the GLABELLA CASTLE can extinguish the eye's light.

questions.q: OnabotulinumtoxinA 100U vial reconstituted with 2.5mL preservative-free normal saline gives which concentration, and what dose is injected per site for the glabellar complex?

2 units per 0.1mL; 20U total for the glabellar complex
1 unit per 0.1mL; 1U per point is sufficient
4 units per 0.1mL; typically 4–5 units per injection point, total 20–25U for glabellar complex

questions.q: Vascular compromise from HA filler injection (blanching, mottling, pain) requires immediate hyaluronidase injection. The recommended initial dose is:

Aspirin 300mg orally first, then hyaluronidase after 2 hours
150 IU after 24 hours to confirm vascular occlusion
300–1500 IU injected immediately into and around the affected area without waiting for confirmation

If ocular symptoms (pain, visual change), refer ophthalmology urgently and give high-dose hyaluronidase retrobulbarly.

questions.q: Low-molecular-weight hyaluronic acid (LMW-HA, <50kDa) in topical formulations differs from HMW-HA (>1000kDa) in which way?
opts: LMW-HA increases TEWL by disrupting the SC barrier; HMW-HA is anti-inflammatory
HMW-HA penetrates deeply while LMW-HA stays entirely on the skin surface
Both forms have identical depth of penetration but differ in water retention capacity only
LMW-HA penetrates the epidermis and may activate pro-inflammatory TLR signalling; HMW-HA forms a superficial film acting as a humectant
questions.exp:

questions.q: Deoxycholic acid (ATX-101 / Kybella) for submental fat reduction causes adipocytolysis by:

Inducing adipocyte apoptosis via caspase-3 activation
Adipocyte cryoapoptosis at subzero temperatures
Detergent-mediated disruption of adipocyte cell membranes causing lysis

questions.q: The original Kligman triple combination formula for melasma contains which three agents and at what concentrations?

Hydroquinone 5% + tretinoin 0.1% + fluocinolone acetonide 0.01%
Kojic acid 2% + glycolic acid 10% + fluticasone 0.05%
Hydroquinone 4% + tretinoin 0.05% + hydrocortisone 1%

🏰 Palace: KLIGMAN's TRIPLE LOCK: 5% HYDROQUINONE KEY + 0.1% TRETINOIN HANDLE + 0.01% FLUOCINOLONE DOORSTOP — the ORIGINAL castle recipe to bleach the melasma gate.

questions.q: Mesotherapy for localised fat reduction classically injects which primary lipolytic agent combination?
opts: L-carnitine alone — mitochondrial fatty acid transport
Phosphatidylcholine (PC) + sodium deoxycholate — membrane disruption causing adipocytolysis
Hyaluronidase — degrades HA scaffolding in adipose tissue
Aminophylline — phosphodiesterase inhibition increasing cAMP

PC disrupts the cell membrane (emulsification), while deoxycholate (a bile acid) potentiates lysis. This combination is also the basis of Kybella (injectable deoxycholate alone). 🏰 Palace: MESOTHERAPY FAT BOMB: PC (the SOAP) + DEOXYCHOLATE (the DETERGENT) together BURST FAT CELL WALLS — one is the WRECKER BALL, the other the WRECKING CREW, and the fat contents SPILL for macrophage cleanup.

questions.q: The 308nm excimer laser achieves repigmentation in vitiligo by which primary mechanism?
opts: Activating MITF directly via UV-induced signalling without melanocyte migration
Stimulating melanocyte migration from perilesional epidermis and hair follicle outer root sheath
Causing DNA damage-induced melanocyte proliferation within vitiligo patches
Reducing CD8+ T-cell density destroying melanocytes within vitiligo
questions.exp:
The 308nm XeCl excimer laser stimulates repigmentation via: (1) immunosuppression (reduces CD4+/CD8+ T cells, reduces TNF-α, IL-17); (2) most importantly, stimulation of melanocyte migration from the outer root sheath (ORS) of hair follicles (the melanocyte reservoir in vitiligo lesions) and from perilesional epidermis. This explains why areas with hair follicles (non-glabrous) respond better and show perifollicular repigmentation first.
🏰 Palace: EXCIMER LASER is the PIED PIPER at 308nm — it calls MELANOCYTE REFUGEES hiding in the HAIR FOLLICLE BUNKERS (ORS) and PERILESIONAL BORDER VILLAGE to MARCH INTO the vitiligo desert and repopulate it.

questions.q: The diode laser at 810nm for hair removal is best suited for which Fitzpatrick skin types and what is its mechanism advantage?
opts: All types equally — the 810nm wavelength bypasses melanin completely
Types V–VI exclusively — at 810nm epidermal melanin is not activated
Types I–II only — highest melanin absorption makes it too risky for darker skin
Types III–IV — intermediate melanin absorption allows effective follicular targeting with manageable epidermal melanin competition
questions.exp:
Diode 810nm occupies the middle ground: higher melanin absorption than Nd:YAG 1064nm (safer for types I–IV) but lower than alexandrite 755nm (safer than alexandrite for types III–IV). Penetration ~3–4mm reaches the follicle bulb. Cooling (contact or cryogen spray) is essential. Compared to alexandrite (safer for I–III) and Nd:YAG (safer for V–VI), diode 810nm is the most versatile mid-range laser.
🏰 Palace: DIODE 810nm is the MIDDLE CHILD of hair removal lasers — HALFWAY between the ALEXANDRITE HUNTER (greedy for melanin) and ND:YAG DEEP DIVER (ignores melanin) — SWEET SPOT for types III–IV skin.

questions.q: Avobenzone (butyl methoxydibenzoylmethane) is an organic UVA filter. Its major photostability problem and the solution are:
opts: Photodegrades rapidly upon UV exposure; stabilised by octocrylene or Helioplex technology
Photodegrades only in water-based formulations; oil-based formulas are stable
Photodegrades only when mixed with titanium dioxide; use zinc oxide instead
Is intrinsically photostable; no stabiliser needed when used alone
questions.exp:
Avobenzone absorbs UVA1 (310–400nm) with peak at 360nm but is photounstable — UV exposure isomerises it from the active enol form to the inactive keto form. It degrades within 15–20 minutes of UV exposure unless stabilised. Stabilisers: octocrylene (energy absorber/quencher), Helioplex (Neutrogena's avobenzone + octocrylene technology), Tinosorb S/M (new-generation stabilised UVA filters). Incompatible with PABA derivatives.
🏰 Palace: AVOBENZONE is the BRAVE UVA GUARD who CRUMBLES after 15 minutes in the sun (photodegrades) unless OCTOCRYLENE BODYGUARD stands beside it — Helioplex puts them in a BULLETPROOF VEST together.

questions.q: In selective photothermolysis, the thermal relaxation time (TRT) of a target structure is proportional to:
opts: The wavelength of the laser used
The absorption coefficient of the target chromophore
The square of the target diameter (TRT ∝ d²) — larger targets need longer pulse durations
The inverse of the target diameter (TRT ∝ 1/d)
questions.exp:
TRT is the time for a target to cool to 50% of its peak temperature after laser heating. TRT is proportional to the SQUARE of the target diameter (TRT ∝ d²). Practical values: melanosomes (~1μm) TRT = ~1μs; hair follicle (~200μm) TRT = ~40–100ms; leg veins (~1mm) TRT = seconds. Pulse duration must be ≤ TRT for selective heating without surrounding tissue damage.
🏰 Palace: TRT grows with the SQUARE of SIZE — a TARGET twice as BIG takes FOUR TIMES LONGER to cool down (2² = 4×). BIG STRUCTURES (leg veins) need LONG PULSES; TINY TARGETS (melanosomes) need ULTRA-SHORT NANOSECOND pulses.

questions.q: The philtrum column injection technique in lip augmentation with HA filler defines which aesthetic structure, and what injection plane is used?

Lip volume — injected submucosally in the wet mucosa
Oral commissures — injected at the corner of the mouth subcutaneously
The nasolabial fold — injected periostally at the pyriform aperture
questions.exp:
Philtrum column technique: HA filler is injected into the vermilion-cutaneous junction (white roll) along the two philtral columns to define the Cupid's bow shape and enhance the cupid's bow peak. Small volumes (0.1–0.2mL per column), superficial intradermal placement. This technique lifts the central Cupid's bow without necessarily adding volume to the lip body.
🏰 Palace: PHILTRUM TOWERS are Cupid's Bow CASTLE TURRETS — inject the WHITE ROLL (vermilion border) like drawing BATTLEMENTS along the two flanking walls to create a DEFINED BOW SHAPE and PRONOUNCED PEAK.

questions.q: Poly-L-lactic acid (PLLA / Sculptra) requires reconstitution with sterile water and a minimum hydration period before injection to prevent nodule formation. The current recommended hydration time is:
opts: 2 hours maximum — do not use after 2 hours
Hydration time does not affect nodule risk; shake vigorously before use
5–10 minutes if mixed with lidocaine
Minimum 24 hours (ideally 48–72 hours) at room temperature before injection
questions.exp:

Current recommendations: reconstitute 5mL vial in 5–8mL sterile water ≥24 hours before use (ideally 48–72h). Extended hydration allows PLLA microspheres to fully hydrate, preventing agglomeration and nodule formation. Lidocaine 1mL added immediately before injection for comfort.
🏰 Palace: SCULPTRA needs a 24–72 HOUR SPA (hydration bath) before entering the face — rush a DRY SCULPTRA into the castle and you get STONE NODULES; give it a long SOAK and it goes in smoothly.

questions.q: A patient taking isotretinoin requests ablative laser resurfacing for acne scars. The recommended minimum waiting period after stopping isotretinoin before ablative procedures is:
opts: 6 months — delayed wound healing and abnormal scarring risk persists up to 6 months post-cessation
1 month — isotretinoin clears within 4 weeks
No waiting period required for non-ablative fractional lasers
3 months — sebaceous gland function normalises by 12 weeks
questions.exp:
The traditional recommendation is a 6-month wait after stopping isotretinoin before any ablative resurfacing. Isotretinoin causes sebaceous gland atrophy, delayed wound healing, and potential for hypertrophic scarring/keloid formation post-laser. Recent evidence suggests non-ablative fractional lasers may be safer at 3–6 months, but most experts still recommend 6 months for ablative CO2/Er:YAG resurfacing.

questions.q: Botulinum toxin treatment for 'gummy smile' (excessive gingival display >2–3mm on smiling) targets which muscle?

Orbicularis oris
Mentalis
Levator labii superioris alaeque nasi (LLSAN) and levator labii superioris (LLS)

questions.q: The Tyndall effect from superficially placed HA filler appears as blue discolouration. Which anatomical level placement causes this, and what treatment reverses it?
opts: Only non-cross-linked HA causes Tyndall effect; cross-linked fillers are exempt
Deep subcutaneous placement of HA causes blue discolouration due to dermal thinning
Superficial intradermal/subdermal placement of HA filler; hyaluronidase injection dissolves the filler
Tyndall effect results from HA filler containing blue dye degradation products
questions.exp:
The Tyndall effect in HA fillers occurs when filler is placed too superficially (intradermal/very superficial subdermal). Light scatters off the HA particles in the dermis; shorter blue wavelengths scatter more (similar to why the sky is blue), producing a bluish hue visible through thin skin. Treatment: hyaluronidase dissolves the filler. Prevention: place HA filler in the correct supraperiosteal, subcutaneous, or deep subdermal plane.
🏰 Palace: TYNDALL TERROR: HA placed TOO SHALLOW in the DERMIS CASTLE becomes a LIGHT-SCATTERING GHOST — blue wavelengths bounce back through THIN SKIN like a BLUE HAUNTING; HYALURONIDASE EXORCIST dissolves the ghost.

questions.q: This pulsed laser handpiece emits yellow light at 585–595 nm and is the gold standard for treating vascular lesions including port wine stains. What physical principle governs its selectivity?
opts: Nd:YAG — targets water at 1064 nm
IPL — targets melanin at 560 nm only
Pulsed Dye Laser (PDL) — selective photothermolysis targeting oxyhaemoglobin at 577–595 nm
CO2 laser — targets haemosiderin at 10,600 nm
questions.exp:
PDL at 585–595 nm targets the Soret/Q-band absorption peaks of oxyhaemoglobin (577 nm, 541 nm). Selective photothermolysis requires wavelength matching the chromophore, pulse duration ≤ thermal relaxation time (TRT) of the target (vessel TRT ∝ vessel diameter²), and sufficient fluence. PDL is the gold standard for port wine stains, haemangiomas, and telangiectasias.

questions.q: For maximum follicular unit graft survival during a hair transplant procedure, grafts should be kept in:
opts: HypoThermosol FRS at room temperature for up to 24 hours
Chilled (4°C) normal saline or Ringer's lactate solution with a maximum out-of-body time of 4–6 hours
Room temperature saline for maximum of 30 minutes

Grafts must never be allowed to dry or be exposed to 37°C.

questions.q: L-ascorbic acid (vitamin C) is most stable and bioavailable in topical formulations at:

pH 5.5–6.5; minimum 5% concentration
pH 7.0; any concentration above 1% penetrates effectively
pH 2.5–3.5; minimum 10% concentration for dermal penetration

questions.q: On the Nürnberger-Müller cellulite grading scale (0–3), Grade II cellulite is characterised by:

Visible deep depressions at rest in any position regardless of posture

questions.q: In PRP for androgenetic alopecia, which growth factor most directly promotes anagen prolongation in dermal papilla cells?
